title: Compound

compareCandidate.label: Compound vs. molecule
compareCandidate.description: A compound is a substance of different elements chemically bonded — its atoms are always different kinds. A molecule is any two or more bonded atoms, same element or different. O₂ is a molecule but not a compound; H₂O is both.

processes: Combining different elements in fixed ratios
Taking on a new identity with new properties
Forming the substances all around us
plainLanguageExplanation: A compound is a substance made when two or more DIFFERENT elements combine by chemical bonding. The key idea: the elements give up their old identities. Take the compound sodium chloride, table salt. It is made of sodium — a soft metal so reactive it fizzes violently in water — and chlorine — a poisonous gas. But bonded together, these two dangerous elements become the safe, tasty crystals you sprinkle on food. The compound has a new identity with new properties. The same is true of water: hydrogen is a flammable gas and oxygen feeds fires, but bonded as H₂O they make the substance that puts fires out. Compounds always have a fixed ratio — water is always exactly two hydrogens to one oxygen. Because the elements are chemically bonded (not just mixed), you cannot separate them by filtering or picking them apart — separating a compound takes a chemical reaction. Compounds are all around us: water, salt, sugar, carbon dioxide, medicines, and the DNA in your cells.

keyFacts.label: What it is
keyFacts.value: A pure substance of two or more different elements chemically bonded

keyFacts.label: New identity
keyFacts.value: Elements lose their old properties — sodium + chlorine becomes safe salt

keyFacts.label: Fixed ratio
keyFacts.value: Always combined in exact proportions — water is always 2H + 1O

keyFacts.label: vs. mixture
keyFacts.value: Bonded, not just mixed — separation needs a chemical reaction

keyFacts.label: Bonds
keyFacts.value: Held by covalent or ionic bonds

whyItMatters: Compounds are almost everything you can name — water, salt, sugar, air's carbon dioxide, medicines, and the molecules of your own body. Understanding compounds explains why matter around you behaves so differently from the raw elements, and it is the door to every chemical reaction and formula in chemistry.
didYouKnow: Hydrogen and oxygen are both gases, but bonded together they make liquid water — a compound with properties neither element has.
compareReason: The molecule-versus-compound split trips up every student — comparing O₂ with H₂O shows precisely where the two ideas diverge.
